name: Resolve identity assurance before device, password, MFA, and account provisioning

attribution.legal_posture: Commercial identity-provider guidance describes control design and availability. It supplies context rather than an incident, adjudication, measured product-efficacy, nationality-determination or named-customer finding.

caveats: The failed, rejected, or inconclusive verification remains a review signal; DPRK affiliation, nationality, identity fraud, and malicious intent require corroborating sources.
A pass or fail result must be reviewable, appealable, privacy-preserving, and combined with document provenance, identity continuity, endpoint custody, role scoping, and post-hire monitoring.
A product recommendation, anomaly, or campaign link is a review input whose significance requires evidence of DPRK affiliation, legal identity, or malicious intent.
Identity review should resolve before initial password creation and MFA enrollment; automated provisioning can accelerate harm when identity assurance, endpoint custody, and role scoping fail.

Accent, appearance, disability accommodations, travel, geography, device replacement, remote work, VPN use, and any single automated signal require a lawful, corroborated basis before they inform risk.
Candidate identities, phone numbers, IP addresses, device selectors, cross-customer graph nodes, and private ATS data are excluded from publication.
Biometric software evaluates liveness or similarity; nationality and DPRK affiliation require cited source evidence.
Face, accent, ethnicity, geography, camera behavior, and any single automated score require human corroboration before an adverse-employment decision.

Every adverse employment or access decision requires trained human review, documented reasons, meaningful correction and appeal, accessible alternatives, proportionality, anti-bias testing, minimization, bounded retention, and legal review.
Nametag is a commercial vendor; its product-efficacy claims await independent validation.
Face, accent, ethnicity, nationality, geography, camera behavior, product result, and single automated signals require corroboration before any adverse-employment or attribution decision.

This record retains no people, personas, accounts, companies, victims, incidents, images, identity documents, biometric material, raw selectors, indicators, file paths, payment details, or private data.
Require trained human review, explainable evidence, data minimization, bounded retention, correction, appeal, accessibility accommodations, and legal review before any adverse decision.
The record describes a defensive control or bounded analytical context; its subject is control/context rather than a person, victim, company, account, or incident profile.
The source describes a commercial product and feature availability; independent effectiveness study and named-customer incident require separate sources.
These are commercial product and integration claims; efficacy and error rates require independent validation.
This exact-ID record adds first-party provenance to an existing review-level control; it extends that control's provenance rather than creating a new control family or actor record.

infrastructure.description: At initial onboarding, do not treat possession of an emailed temporary password or pre-signed link as sufficient proof that the approved hire is setting up the account. Use a separately reviewable identity-continuity step before first password selection and MFA enrollment, with documented exceptions, appeal, accessible alternatives, minimization, and retention limits.

Nametag recommends inserting an identity-assurance gate at new-hire account provisioning: resolve the organization's verification workflow before the person connects a new device, sets an initial password, or enrolls an MFA factor. Abstracted from the product claim, this is a useful control boundary because a failed or unresolved identity check cannot automatically become a fully provisioned workforce identity.

sources.support: The blog says the product analyzes new ATS identities, correlates behavioral, identity, and threat-intelligence signals, groups linked candidates into campaigns, creates evidence timelines, and supports review before provisioning. The press release states July 28 announcement and August 3 availability. Evidence boundary: Provider description of its own product and detection model. DPRK case scale and consequences are derivative of public official reporting; no named customer incident or independently measured efficacy is disclosed. Normalized use: review identities at the ATS/pre-provisioning boundary and retain a sourced evidence timeline for trained human review; do not treat a product flag as attribution or an employment decision

sources.support: Nametag describes replacing temporary passwords and pre-signed onboarding links with a flow that verifies a new hire before allowing initial password setting and MFA enrollment. The page explicitly markets the control for North Korean IT-worker impersonation risk. Evidence boundary: provider-described control design; not an incident report or independent efficacy study Normalized control: At initial onboarding, do not treat possession of an emailed temporary password or pre-signed link as sufficient proof that the approved hire is setting up the account. Use a separately reviewable identity-continuity step before first password selection and MFA enrollment, with documented exceptions, appeal, accessible alternatives, minimization, and retention limits. Limitations: This is a vendor product claim, not an independently measured effectiveness result. Identity verification must not become nationality inference or a biometrics-only employment gate. Organizations need notice, proportionality, human review, correction and appeal, accessible alternatives, retention controls, and legal review. A failed or incomplete check is not proof of DPRK affiliation or malicious intent
